briefs.source_chain: The Fed's tightening case predated the oil shock (Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks + broadening inflation pressure) therefore a Houthi-driven Strait-of-Hormuz oil shock (Brent >$100) reinforced rather than caused the hawkish path, feeding CPI/PPI upside and a BoE rate-risk citation, so the FOMC hiked 25bp unanimously with Warsh signaling more tightening; equities sold off intraday then recovered the following session as yields/oil eased and flows rotated back to AI tech, helped by a year of earnings outpacing price gains that compressed the forward P/E (23x to 19.1x), leaving room to absorb higher rates; the BoJ hiked to a 31-year high but the yen still weakened as the widening Fed-BoJ gap and a split vote kept carry trades intact; the bank stays neutral equities, constructive earnings against higher real-rate risk.
